subject: Future Tech
title: Classical Bits vs Qubits
description: A quick, practical guide to Classical Bits vs Qubits.

hook.text: A classical bit is either 0 or 1, like a light switch. A qubit can be 0, 1, or a blend of both simultaneously.

buildup.text: Two classical bits hold one of four states. Two qubits hold all four states at the same time.

discovery.text: With ten qubits you can represent 1,024 states at once. Classical bits would need to check each one separately.

twist.text: But reading a qubit collapses its superposition. You only get one answer, so algorithms must be cleverly designed.

climax.text: Quantum speedup comes from interference: amplifying right answers and canceling wrong ones before measurement.

punchline.text: One qubit holds two worlds at once.

quiz.question: How many states can two qubits represent simultaneously?
